messages:
elaine-cs: FYI — customer VideoAI reporting a burst of 504/gateway timeouts during a tenant spike at ~17:03 UTC. ~20% of requests failing, escalation opened by AE. Logs attached.

sam-oncall: ACK. Pinging @deven-sre and @maria-eng to triage. Any quick mitigation we can push? :eyes:

deven-sre: On it. Can you paste a couple example trace ids + tenant id? Also which region?

elaine-cs: tenant: videoai-prod, traces: 9f1c2a3e, 9f1c2b4f. Gateway logs show upstream timeout and long queue times: ```
[2026-03-17T17:03:12Z] gateway-req-id=9f1c2a3e tenant=videoai-prod upstream=504 timeout=30s queue_wait=22s
```

deven-sre: Looking at cluster metrics — these 504s line up with pod spin-up windows. HPA + KEDA events around that time. Running `kubectl describe scaledobject videoai-scaledobject -n inference` shows frequent scale-to-zero and then slow restore. Snippet: ```
Triggers: external Kafka (queue length) pollingInterval: 30s cooldownPeriod: 60s minReplicaCount: 0 maxReplicaCount: 10
```
This means we often have 0 pods when a burst hits => coldstarts.

maria-eng: Adding that model (video-embedder-v2) has heavier init after last deploy — model init ~20-30s (weights + mmap fallback). Readiness probe blocks until model loaded, so first requests queue. Pod logs: ```
2026-03-17T17:02:55Z INFO model-loader: loading weights (1.2GB)
2026-03-17T17:03:15Z INFO model-loader: kv-cache init complete, ready
```
So cold-start time ~20s. With KEDA polling 30s, often the scaler doesn't trigger fast enough and gateway times out.

jordan-ml: Confirmed from profiling — quant fallback path increases load latency. For heavy models we recommend prewarm replicas or allow pinned warm pool. If `redwood.ai/prewarm` is disabled for the tenant then no prewarm will run.

deven-sre: I just checked tenant annotations — videoai-prod had `redwood.ai/prewarm: "false"` and `redwood.ai/minReplicas: "0"` on their pool. Combined with KEDA cooldown/minReplica=0 = scale-to-zero behaviour. Also KEDA ScaledObject pollingInterval=30s + cooldown 60s creates blind windows. YAML excerpt: ```
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: videoai-scaledobject
spec:
  pollingInterval: 30
  cooldownPeriod: 60
  minReplicaCount: 0
  triggers: [ ... ]
```

elaine-cs: Customer says this regressed after yesterday's environment changes. They ran some integration tests and began seeing 504s on first heavy-rps wave.

sam-oncall: Short-term mitigation plan: 1) enable prewarm for tenant, 2) set minReplicaCount to 1 for the tenant pool, 3) reduce KEDA pollingInterval temporarily to 5s or add a webhook-based trigger to detect burst faster. Can ops patch quickly?

deven-sre: Patching now: `kubectl annotate tenant videoai-prod redwood.ai/prewarm=enabled --overwrite` and `kubectl patch scaledobject videoai-scaledobject -n inference --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1}}'`. Also creating a temporary HPA override to target 1 replica. Executing...

ops-bot: [automated] Patch rollout started: patch/videoai-scaledobject at 7054322050 by deven-sre.

maria-eng: After enabling prewarm & minReplica=1, quick metrics show scale-up latency for first request dropped from ~28s to ~6s. Gateway 504s dropped dramatically. Still seeing intermittent 5xx during high-concurrency bursts because queue backlog + token-throttles can spike when many concurrent cold requests arrive.

sam-oncall: Good. Elaine — please update customer that we've applied a temporary fix and are monitoring. Recommend telling them we will fully tune scaler parameters and tenant defaults tomorrow.

elaine-cs: Customer notified: "Thanks, we see errors decreasing. Please keep us posted on full fix ETA."

deven-sre: Next steps / full fix plan: 
- Adjust KEDA ScaledObject pollingInterval -> 5s for bursty tenants OR switch to webhook trigger on queue.len metric.
- Set tenant template to `prewarm: enabled` for models with init > 10s.
- Add stabilizationWindow / scalingPolicy to HPA to avoid flapping and allow warmup window.
- Increase readinessProbe timeout to 45s for heavy models and add a soft-success endpoint that returns 202 until KV-cache primed.
- Add runbook steps for support to bump minReplica for customer-facing tenants.

maria-eng: I'll open PR to change default tenant template and add telemetry for model-init durations. jordan-ml will add an ML-side change to reduce quant-fallback time.

deven-sre: Repro steps for oncall/docs (put in incident runbook):
1) `kubectl annotate tenant videoai-prod redwood.ai/prewarm=enabled`
2) `kubectl patch scaledobject videoai-scaledobject -n inference --type merge -p '{"spec":{"minReplicaCount":1}}'`
3) Run burst load: ```bash
for i in {1..200}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"x"}' &
done
wait
```
4) Observe pods: `kubectl get hpa,deploy,po -n inference -w`
5) Roll back patch after monitoring or make permanent change via tenant template.

jordan-ml: Also filing PR to add `redwood.ai/prewarm: enabled` to templates for any model where `model_init_seconds > 10`.

elaine-cs: Customer reports error rate down to <1% after temporary patch. They asked for the root cause summary and the permanent plan — I provided today's actions + tomorrow's work.

sam-oncall: Please add a follow-up ticket to infra board to audit tenants with prewarm disabled and list high-init models. Also capture a checklist for oncall to run when a tenant reports burst 504s.

deven-sre: Created INF-7123 with links to this thread and the reproduction steps.

elaine-cs: Marking as resolved for now, will keep monitoring for 24h. Customer happy for immediate support. :white_check_mark:

jordan-ml: Note for later — we should investigate faster memory-mapped loading and overlapping KV-cache population to shave 10-15s off cold-init.

elaine-cs: Thanks team. Closing the thread once INF-7123 has update.
